title: Joanap: the FBI maps a hidden botnet

scenes.narration: [serious] To catch hackers, the FBI pretended to be their victims.
Hackers had taken over many computers around the world. Together, they formed a secret army. Its name was Joanap.
The army spread by itself, from computer to computer. Each one obeyed the hackers. America blamed North Korea.
The problem? This army had no boss computer. The computers only talked to each other.
So in 2019, a judge said yes. The FBI set up fake victim computers. Real infected computers called them.
Now the FBI could see every computer in the army. The owners were warned.
To beat the army, the FBI joined it.

facts.claim: On January 30, 2019 the Justice Department announced a court-authorized effort to map and disrupt the Joanap botnet, using search warrants and court orders under Rule 41
Joanap gives root-level remote control of Windows computers, is peer-to-peer with no central server, is spread by the Brambul worm, and has operated since 2009
The FBI and the Air Force Office of Special Investigations ran servers that mimicked infected peers, collecting IP addresses, ports and timestamps to map the botnet
U.S. victims were notified through their ISPs; foreign victims through their governments
U.S. officials attributed Joanap to the North Korean government; North Korean programmer Park Jin Hyok was charged in 2018 in a complaint alleging a conspiracy that used Brambul

seo.title: Joanap Botnet: How the FBI Posed as Victims to Map North Korea's Army
seo.description: In 2019 the FBI and Air Force investigators, with court approval, ran fake infected computers inside the Joanap botnet. It revealed the victims of a network U.S. officials blame on North Korea. Learn how the FBI took down part of the Joanap botnet. #cybersecurity #fbi #botnet #shorts
